scope: The two placement rows this package publishes — forge.trigger.equipment.deploy_completed and forge.trigger.equipment.recall_completed — read from the deployed world object's own spawn and pickup bodies, plus the port that tells a sentry from a mine.

used.name: Modules-ASM.dll
used.readWith: the local decompilation of the shipped interop assembly (%TEMP%\covtrigb\ilspy\Modules), read-only; the same assembly hash w4-deployable-hooks.json and deployable-life-facts.json were read from

interop.whyInteropIsNotBodies: Every game member in an interop assembly is a wrapper around IL2CPP.il2cpp_runtime_invoke. The interop therefore fixes a member's exact name, declaring type, parameter list, return type, slot and virtual/override status, and it proves nothing about what the native body does. Every statement below about what a body does is taken from the call graph already frozen in evidence/w4-deployable-hooks.json (dumper dump.cs of the same build), never from interop.
interop.il2cppWrapperSituation: Harmony reaches a native method through the metadata token the interop's own static constructor resolves, so a private native body is a patch target exactly like a public one, and a field is read through IL2CPP.il2cpp_field_get_offset, so a private field is readable. A wrapper never exposes a body, so nothing here claims what a body does beyond the frozen call graph.

grounds: w4-deployable-hooks.json method sentry-instance-spawn: rva 0x14184B0, rvaSharing 1, slot 150, body 1140 B, direct callers none, calls PlayerBackpack::SetDeployed at site 0x1418870.
Slot 150 with no literal caller is the replication path: the world object is created from the gear spawn data, not by the placement code, so the body runs on every end that holds the object.
hooks.fact: forge.trigger.equipment.deploy_completed with equipment_kind = sentry_gun. It is also one of exactly three bodies in this build that write the owning backpack's deployed marker (w4-deployable-hooks.json backpack-set-deployed lists PlaceOnGround, this one and SyncedPickup).

grounds: w4-deployable-hooks.json method mine-spawn: rva 0x14FFEF0, rvaSharing 1, slot 150, body 585 B, direct callers none, calls its own OnSpawnData.
Same slot and same IDynamicReplicatorSupplier<pItemSpawnData> shape as the sentry, so the mine's world object also exists through the replication path.
hooks.fact: forge.trigger.equipment.deploy_completed with equipment_kind = mine. It is the only deploy signal the two families share: neither MineDeployerInstance.OnSpawn nor its SyncedPickup writes the backpack marker (the marker's three decoded call sites are all sentry bodies).

grounds: w4-deployable-hooks.json method sentry-instance-pickup: rva 0x141B2B0, rvaSharing 1, slot 45, virtual override, body 1406 B, direct callers none, calls PlayerAgent::get_Owner, its own get_Replicator and PlayerBackpack::SetDeployed at site 0x141B687.
Slot 45 of ISyncedItem, reached through interface dispatch, and it carries the acting player as its own parameter.
hooks.fact: forge.trigger.equipment.recall_completed with equipment_kind = sentry_gun. The acting player is the game's own parameter, not a value this package derives.

grounds: w4-deployable-hooks.json method mine-pickup: rva 0x1500600, rvaSharing 1, slot 45, virtual override, body 489 B, direct callers none, calls PlayerAgent::get_Owner and nothing else.
hooks.fact: forge.trigger.equipment.recall_completed with equipment_kind = mine. The mine never writes the backpack deployed marker, so this body is the mine's only recall signal.

hooks.interopSignature: public override void OnDespawn(); public new void OnDestroy()

kind.question: How does one placement fact say whether it is a sentry or a mine?
kind.answer: The hook class declares it. The spawning body is the family's own class — SentryGunInstance or MineDeployerInstance, two classes with no inheritance relation and one placement body each — so the class the patch targets is the answer, and this package stores it on the placement it mints.
grounds: The interop declares `public class SentryGunInstance : ItemEquippable, IDynamicReplicatorSupplier<pGearSpawnData>, ...` and `public class MineDeployerInstance : ItemEquippable, IDynamicReplicatorSupplier<pItemSpawnData>, ...`; neither derives from the other.

No instance member of either class names the shell: the two deployed types share the Item/ItemEquippable surface, and the backpack slot that placed them holds the first-person tool class (SentryGunFirstPerson / MineDeployerFirstPerson), which is a third pair of classes.
kind.wireForm: The port is the framework's closed enum set `equipment_kind`, so a fact carries the member's compiled index; the framework resolves it back to the member name at the handler boundary (RuntimeJson.EnumPortToHandlerValue).
kind.markerPathKinds: The backpack-marker path needs the kind before any spawn is seen, so it resolves the same five classes through the interop cast: the two first-person tools (the classes a placement slot actually holds while the tool is still in hand) and the two deployed instances (the classes a fixture and a replayed readback hold). A slot holding anything else is not a placement this package can name and mints none.

authority.question: Which machine observes a placement, and does the host see a client's?
authority.answer: Every machine that holds the world object observes it there, and only the host publishes.
grounds: w4-deployable-hooks.json authority: both ends hold a SentryGunInstance; it is an IDynamicReplicatorSupplier<pGearSpawnData> whose world object is created through the item replication path (OnSpawn, slot 150), and the host is authoritative for the simulation.
ForgeWeapon/Native/EquipmentNativeAdapter.Authoritative requires SNet.IsMaster, a Ready runtime and IsHost == true, so a client-side replica's observation publishes nothing.
The spawn body runs on every end because the replication machinery invokes it, not the placement code (no literal caller at slot 150).
consequences: A host sees a client's placement at the client's replicated world instance spawn, which is the deploy signal both families share.

The client's own backpack marker write (PlayerBackpack::SetDeployed at PlaceOnGround) is local state on the placer's machine; it is not one of the replicated members this evidence decodes. The world instance is therefore what this package joins the placement to on a machine that did not run the placement, and the join is by the owner the replicated instance itself reports.

unverified.statement: Whether PlayerBackpack::SetDeployed runs on the host for a slot a client deployed.
unverified.reason: The metadata fixes the three call sites but not who invokes them, and the backpack item's replication is an item packet rather than a marker write. Nothing decoded here says the marker crosses machines.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime trace on a host with one client deploying a sentry, reading IsDeployed for that client's slot before and after.

unverified.statement: Whether a sentry's world spawn or its owner's marker write arrives first on the placer's own machine.
unverified.reason: Both orders are legal in the decoded call graph, and the two are the same event seen from two places.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime counter on both bodies across one placement; the observer is idempotent by construction, so only the diagnostic line differs.

unverified.statement: Whether the recall pickup runs before the world object's OnDespawn / OnDestroy on every machine.
unverified.reason: w4-deployable-hooks.json records SyncedPickup and the two ending bodies as separate paths with no decoded order between them.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime trace of one recall on the host and on the recalling client.

unverified.statement: Whether the mine writes any backpack state at pickup that a reader could use instead of the world object.
unverified.reason: MineDeployerInstance declares neither SyncedTurnOn nor SyncedTurnOff, and its SyncedPickup body calls only PlayerAgent::get_Owner.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A decompilation of the mine's own Setup / Update path, or a runtime probe of the pickup interaction.

limits: No claim about runtime behaviour: nothing here was executed; every member list was read from a local decompilation of the shipped interop assembly and of the build's own dump.
A member that exists in the interop is a member this build has; it does not prove the body runs on a given machine or how often.

The zone a placement stands in is not published on either row: a level's zone is a map-domain resource read through forge.selector.target.zone for any entity, and this row carries the placement's own position as the anchor that query is asked about.
